newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: Court restricts member states' right to deny aid.
newsitem.headline: Court restricts member states' right to deny aid.

text.p: The European Court of Justice ruled on Thursday that member states may not condition aid to farmers under the "extensification of production programme" on reduced output except during defined reference periods.

Community regulations require member states to create aid schemes for production in certain sectors showing surpluses, particularly in the beef and veal sectors, to promote the "extensification" of production.

"Extensification" is defined as a reduction of at least 20 percent, for a period of at least five years, in the output of the product concerned, without any increase in other surplus production capacity.
Under the regulation, reduction in output is ensured by farmers and is calculated in relation to average annual output over a designated reference period.

In the case at hand, Italy considered production during an intermediate period, after the end of a reference period, and before the period of the farmer's commitment. The court ruled that Community rules do not allow member states to consider fluctuations in output during this intermediate period.
(Court translation into English. Original language of the case: Italian)
"Aid to promote the extensification of agricultural production - Calculation of reduction in output - Reference period"
Reference by the Consiglio di Stato (Italy) for a preliminary ruling in the proceedings pending before that court between

on the interpretation of Council regulation (EEC) No 797/85 of 12 March 1985 on improving the efficiency of agricultural structures (OJ 1985 L 93, p. 1), as amended by Council regulation (EEC) No 1760/87 of 15 June 1987 (OJ 1987 L 167, p. 1), and as both amended by Council regulation (EEC) No 1094/88 of 25 April 1988 (OJ 1988 L 106, p. 28), and of Commission regulation (EEC) No 4115/88 of 21 December 1988 laying down detailed rules for applying the aid scheme to promote the extensification of production (OJ 1988 L 361, p. 13),

Article 1b(3)(c) of Council regulation (EEC) No 797/85 of 12 March 1985 on improving the efficiency of agricultural structures, as amended by Council regulation (EEC) No 1760/87 of 15 June 1987, and as both amended by Council regulation (EEC) No 1094/88 of 25 April 1988, and of Commission regulation (EEC) No 4115/88 of 21 December 1988 laying down detailed rules for applying the aid scheme to promote the extensification of production must be interpreted as not allowing a member state, where there has been a drop in output during the intermediate period between the end of the reference period and the beginning of the period of the undertaking, to make the grant of aid for "extensification" in any case conditional on output achieved during the intermediate period being reduced, during the period of the undertaking, by an amount corresponding to at least 20 percent of output during the reference period.
